fix(T2.23): RFC 4180 line endings so embedded CR is quoted on every Python

csv.writer only quotes fields containing a character of its line
terminator. With "\n", a value containing a bare CR was written
unquoted on CI's Pythons, producing a broken row; local 3.14.3 happened
to quote it. "\r\n" (the CSV standard, and what spreadsheets expect)
quotes both. A new test keeps CR/LF inside their cell, checked on a real
3.10.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs(release): publish the untagged draft by ID via the API

gh release edit takes a tag name, and the draft no longer has a tag, so
step 8 now finds the draft's ID and PATCHes the release.

Addresses Copilot review on #46.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

chore(release): 1.4.0 "One CLI"

feat: show original filenames in previews and reports (#38)

On current macOS ZASSET.ZFILENAME is Photos' internal storage name (a
UUID), so a real library's cleanup preview listed "B3E2E2AA-….jpeg" and
the user couldn't tell what they were approving.

- _common: original_filename_sql(schema) selects
  ZADDITIONALASSETATTRIBUTES.ZORIGINALFILENAME as original_filename (NULL
  when absent), and build_asset_query includes it. display_name(item)
  prefers it over filename.
- All 16 scripts that list files add original_filename to their items,
  declare an optional "original_filenames" section (ORIGINAL_FILENAME
  group), and print display_name() in --human output. cleanup_executor,
  smart_export, scene_search (search mode only) and storage_analyzer gain
  a Degradation so a missing column is reported.
- filename is unchanged and stays the AppleScript identity cross-check;
  a test pins that the display name never reaches the script.

Tests: tests/test_original_filenames.py (UUID storage names plus real
original names, as on modern libraries), and the degradation sweep's
rich fixture gains the column.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(T1.8): --quiet drops diagnostics, never the result

Addresses Copilot review on #48.

- cleanup_executor with no candidates: in human mode the message is the
  result, so it goes to stdout even with --quiet (before, both streams
  were empty). JSON mode is unchanged: JSON on stdout, with a stderr
  note unless --quiet.
- smart_export: the final "Export complete" counts went to the progress
  stream, which --quiet discards. In human mode they now print to stdout
  (in JSON mode they're in the result), and skipped items are reported
  on stderr in both formats as a problem.

Regression tests fail before this change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

perf: load index labels only for the photos a run shows

Addresses Copilot review on #51: the first top() loaded every asset's
labels, so on_this_day (a few photos) decoded and cached the whole
library's label associations.

- SearchIndex.labels_for_uuids(uuids) reads labels for just those UUIDs,
  in chunked `uuid_0 IN (...)` queries on the assets index, filtering
  uuid_1 in Python. It replaces the whole-library labels_by_uuid.
- IndexLabels.preload(ids) loads a batch once; timeline_recap preloads
  every photo in the timeline and on_this_day every photo across the
  years shown. top() only counts in memory and loads anything missing.

The synthetic 2,000-event timeline stays at 0.04 s. A new test checks
on_this_day asks the index about exactly the photos it shows (2 of 4).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(T1.7): envelope leads in Markdown and survives in CSV

Addresses Copilot review on #50.

- Markdown rendered every scalar before any list, so a command's own
  fields (e.g. smart_export's output_dir/exported) came before
  `warnings`. The envelope is now rendered as its own leading block.
- CSV only collected lists of objects, so the envelope vanished and an
  empty result was a bare header. A first `section=envelope` row now
  carries schema_version/command/generated_at; warnings follow as
  `warnings` rows. ENVELOPE_KEYS names the fields once.

Tests cover Markdown order with empty and populated warnings, CSV
metadata for an empty result, warnings as rows, and the per-command
CSV check now expects the envelope row (4 fail before this change).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge pull request #49 from and3rn3t/feat/t2.23-md-csv-output

feat(T2.23): --format md|csv for every command

fix(T2.23): neutralize CSV formulas; keep `section` as the source path

Addresses Copilot review on #49.

- CSV injection: album titles, filenames and names come from the
  library, i.e. from whoever shared a photo. A text cell starting with
  = + - @, tab or CR now gets a leading apostrophe, so a spreadsheet
  shows it instead of running it. Numbers (e.g. -33.86 latitude) and the
  JSON/Markdown formats are untouched. Recorded in the threat model.
- `section` always holds the row's source path. A payload field named
  `section` (degraded entries, doctor's degraded_sections) used to
  overwrite it and is now kept as `entry_section`.

Regression tests (TestCsvInjection, hostile album title end to end,
nonempty degraded): 9 fail before this change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
